text:
maria-finance: FYI vendor CorkData Co-op (vendor_id CD-310) submitted INV-IE-2025-909 on 2025-07-14 and charged Irish VAT plus a 3% "gross-up" line citing potential backup withholding. Invoice addressed to Redwood, Inc (US) but PO 6222 is under Redwood Ltd (GB). Can tax/legal confirm next steps?
ethan-procurement: Which entity did PO target?
maria-finance: PO 6222 is for Redwood Ltd (GB987654321). Invoice excerpt:
```Invoice: INV-IE-2025-909
Vendor: CorkData Co-op (IE)
VAT reg: IE1234567FH
Service: Data pipeline audit (June 2025) 30h @ €150 = €4,500
Gross-up (tax indemnity) 3% = €135
VAT 23% = €1,051.05
Total = €5,686.05```
kevin-legal: Strange. Irish VAT charged to a UK business may be unnecessary if reverse charge applies. Also "gross-up" as tax indemnity needs contract backing. The backup withholding claim is odd: W-9 is for US payees to provide TIN to US payers. Vendor can't ask us for a W-9 to avoid their own withholdings.
tax-bot: Automated check: vendor country=IE. No W-8/W-9 on vendor file. PO entity matches Redwood Ltd VAT GB987654321. Note: reverse charge for B2B services typically applies within EU/UK context; because vendor invoiced US entity we need reissue to UK entity. Gross-up clause not present in SOW 3.1.
maria-finance: AP placed invoice ON_HOLD in Coupa. Tagging procurement to request reissue + supporting docs.
ethan-procurement: Reached out to CorkData: asked for reissued invoice to Redwood Ltd (GB VAT), explanation for Irish VAT (are they registered and why charging a UK company), removal of gross-up unless contractually agreed, and clarification on backup withholding claim (they referenced "US backup withholding if payer is US entity"). Asked them to upload any tax forms to vendor portal: https://vendor.redwood.example/upload
vendor-cork: (reply captured) "Apologies - our billing team auto-billed US by mistake and applied VAT. We also added 3% to cover a corporate tax withholding that our accountant fears will be applied by US banks. Can you provide a W-9 so we can evidence your US tax status?"
kevin-legal: Responded to vendor: No W-9 needed from Redwood Ltd. If you bill Redwood Ltd we will provide our UK VAT and you should apply reverse charge where appropriate or zero-rate if charity/co-op rules apply. The W-9 request is misdirected; W-9 is for US payees. If vendor expects withholding by their bank, they must provide local evidence and a tax voucher. Gross-up must be supported by signed amendment.
tax-bot: Guidance: 1) Request reissue to Redwood Ltd (GB987654321). 2) Ask vendor to remove VAT if reverse charge applies or explain why domestic VAT is charged. 3) Deny gross-up unless contractually documented. 4) If vendor claims bank-level withholding, require official bank/tax documentation showing authority and amount. 5) No W-8/W-9 needed for an Irish supplier billing a UK company; W-8BEN-E only if vendor is foreign for US reporting when Redwood (US) pays them and treaty benefits claimed.
maria-finance: Draft email posted for review: ```Hi CorkData billing,
PO 6222 is for Redwood Ltd (VAT GB987654321). Please reissue the invoice addressed to Redwood Ltd and either remove Irish VAT or include a clear reverse-charge note if appropriate. Also remove the 3% gross-up unless you can provide a signed SOW amendment authorizing it. If you expect any bank withholding, please provide official documentation from your bank/tax authority showing the basis. Payment will be on hold until we receive corrected invoice and supporting docs.
Thanks, Maria (Finance)```
ethan-procurement: Sent 2025-07-14 11:03 BST.
payments-bot: Invoice INV-IE-2025-909 flagged ON_HOLD at 2025-07-14T11:05:00Z by maria-finance.
vendor-cork: Vendor replied 2025-07-14 14:20 BST: "Will reissue to Redwood Ltd and remove gross-up. Our bank said some US payers' intermediaries sometimes apply backup withholding; we'll provide a written note from our bank if that occurs."
maria-finance: Marking for follow-up. Once reissued invoice (no VAT/gross-up or with reverse charge note) is uploaded we can clear hold. Keep copies for audit.
